title: Adaptive ingest and prioritization ladder for data control & export requests
creator: Asha Menon
description: Create an operational playbook and automated intake ladder for non-bug customer requests related to data governance controls (logging redaction, retention tuning, PII handling, and audit exports). Goal: standardize intake, generate an impact-adjusted priority score, route to the correct owning team (Security, Platform, or Solutions), and attach a clear SLA, cost estimate, and rollout path. The playbook must be lightweight enough for self-serve by Solutions or CSMs but rigorous enough to feed engineering planning and legal/compliance reviews.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form template implemented in Zendesk/Confluence with required + optional fields
Priority ladder computes a stable score and maps to routing buckets: Fast Track, Standard, Compliance Escalation
Automated routing rules created (Slack alerts + Tickets created in Engineering or Security queues)
SLA table published with response and resolution targets per bucket (and visible to customers)
Pilot with 3 enterprise customers completed and feedback documented
Runbook for data-handling steps and encryption/KMS checkpoints reviewed by Security
intake_form_fields: Request type: redaction | retention | PII-handling | audit-export | other
Samples: affected logs/datasets (scrubbed) or example rows
Regulatory driver (HIPAA, GDPR, CCPA, SOC2, other)
Production impact: user-facing outage risk or data exposure risk
Data residency constraints and export locations
Preferred solution approach (config change | RBAC | export tooling | offline batch)
Cost sensitivity and budget owner contact
scoring_matrix: Compliance driver: 40 points if required by law or contractual clause
Production impact: 20 points if affects SLOs or exposes PII
Strategic value: 10 points for logo/ARR > $100k or high-priority channel partner
Final score buckets: >=80 Fast Track (24-72h response), 50-79 Standard (5-10 business days), <50 Backlog (stakeholder sync)
routing_rules: If Compliance driver flagged -> route to Security SRE + Legal for triage (Compliance Escalation)
If request is retention-only with no PII -> route to Platform Ops with automation playbook
If data export request with cross-border transfers -> route to Privacy + Solutions Engineer
If redaction required across persistent KV caching or model inputs -> route to Serving Runtime team + Security
If customer has Dedicated or Private deployment -> include their Cloud/Infra owner and enable direct ticketing to Dedicated support
sla_targets: Fast Track: initial response within 24h, triage call within 48h, fix or mitigation plan within 72h
Standard: initial response within 3 business days, plan within 7 business days
Backlog: acknowledgement within 5 business days, scheduled into roadmap or queued for next cycle

Engineering effort underestimated for runtime-level redaction leading to latency regressions
Legal/regulatory requirements could force emergency work and reorder roadmap
Inconsistent routing may leak sensitive requests to wrong queues

sample_decision_flow: 1) Intake received -> compute score -> display bucket to triage owner
2) If Compliance Escalation -> immediate Security + Legal review within 24h
3) If Fast Track -> assign to on-call engineer + mitigation plan within 72h
4) If Standard -> schedule in next available prioritization cycle and notify CS
5) After remediation, run post-change checklist: perf tests, audit log of change, customer confirmation
